CLASS_TUTORIALS.//: Cam (2026-10-17): every tutor offers a lesson -- 'all basic provisions and how to do everything related to that class. Inclusive of poison making, weapon crafting, holy water, etc.' -- and a starter kit in a wooden crate at the end. Kits: the Game Developer with the Economist (Collaboration N3); stories: the Narrative Designer (each tutor leaves for their real master -- threads for the story re-work, N2). A step: say, then a job (check), a thing to make (make + ws: for real if the bench is open to you, else the tutor makes it -- show -- and says what opens it), or just words. gift: given on the step, once per class ever. items: lent at the start. gifts + kit: the farewell. Checks: wear:<item>, ranged, magic, dual, shield, coat, bless, brew, special, loadout, tools, made:<item>, skill:<skill>, hunt:<n>, crook, train, fed, pack.

hunter.title: Hunter tutor
hunter.goodbye: Watch the treeline, and don't touch Ash's snares.

kit.name: Hunter's starter crate
kit.about: Wren's parting gift: a quiver, arrows, snares and nets, and the Hunter's book.

say: Wren. Ash's apprentice -- he's away, so you get me. You've taken the Hunter's road: shall I show you how it works? It won't take long, and I'll lend you what you need.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
Ash said you'd come. He's out past the Forest after something big -- he left me to start you off, and then I'm to catch him up, so let's not dawdle.

The Hunter's road is patience: a bow, a knife for when the arrows run out, and a trap for anything that thinks it's quicker than you. Everything you need today is in your bag -- a short bow, sixty improvised arrows, a quiver to carry them and a knife.

Quiver first: arrows only go in a quiver -- no quiver, no arrows. Wear the improvised one. It only holds arrows you make yourself; a leather quiver holds far more, and bronze, when you're ready for it.
Now the bow. Put the short bow in your hand and the improvised arrows in your quiver -- your Character sheet, Gear, click a slot on your figure.
Arrows run out. A Hunter with a knife never does: in your bag, use your knife on twigs (or an oak log) to whittle arrow shafts.
Here's a bundle of twigs. Open your bag, choose Use with... on the twigs, and whittle.
A shaft and some leaf litter for flights makes an improvised arrow. Poor, but it flies -- and leaf litter falls in every twiggy wood.
Use a shaft with the leaf litter I've given you.
Now the clever part. A trap holds a creature for a round or two; a net slows it. Your hunt plan decides which you take into a fight -- set it on your Character sheet's Combat tab.
I've given you three twig snares and a twine net. Choose them in your plan.
steps.goal: Choose a trap or a net in your hunt plan

say: You'll go through snares. A twig snare is six twigs and a thread at the crafting bench -- here are the makings.
When your special bar fills in a fight, a Hunter has two tricks: an Aimed shot (far likelier to hit, double damage, two arrows) and a Volley (three arrows at once).
Pick one on the Combat tab -- it fires itself when the bar is full, or press it yourself in a fight you're playing.
Now let's see it. The Farmyard's hunting ground -- win three fights. Keep an eye on your arrows; if they run low, come home and whittle.
That'll do. You'll make a Hunter yet.

I'm off after Ash -- he's three days ahead and he never waits. Take this crate: a proper quiver, arrows, snares, nets, and the Hunter's book. Read the book; it's everything I'd tell you if I had the time.

berserker.title: Berserker tutor
berserker.goodbye: Hit first. Hit hardest. Don't stop.

kit.name: Berserker's starter crate
kit.about: Brakka's parting gift: a maul, brews, food and the Berserker's book.

say: Brakka. You've picked the Berserker's road -- good choice, the only choice. Want me to show you how it's done? I'll lend you the iron.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
Thorvald's in the north with the cold and the yaks. He'll send for me soon -- until then, you're mine.

The Berserker's road is simple: hit it, get hit, get angrier. Every blow you take fills your fury, and fury pays for your specials. I've put a longsword, spiked gauntlets and two Berserker brews in your bag.
A longsword. Heavier than a sword, harder than a sword, and only a Berserker swings one. Put it in your hand.
Spiked gauntlets on your hands -- your figure's arms slot: a punch with them can open a bleed. And if your sword breaks mid-fight, they're still there.
Your weapons are forged at the anvil -- longswords, mauls, spiked gauntlets, all of it. A maul hits harder still. Here's bronze and oak: forge one.

Fury. It fills as you're hit and as you hit. Spend it on Cleave (a heavy swing), Rage (two and a half times the damage -- but you take more this fight) or Bloodlust (you heal from what you deal). Choose one on the Combat tab.
A Berserker brew: more attack and a harder hit, for thirty blows. Drink one before a big fight -- from your bag.
You'll brew your own at the apothecary table one day, from mandrake, rosemary and truffles. That's a long way off.
Go on then. The Farmyard. Three fights. Don't run.
Ha! That's the stuff.

Thorvald's sent word -- the yaks are restless and so am I. I'm away north. Here: a maul, more brews, bronze and oak for the anvil, food, and the Berserker's book. Don't read it in front of Wren, she'll never let you forget it.

kit.name: Arcane's starter crate
kit.about: Ilse's parting gift: runes of every element, essence stones and the Arcane's book.

say: Ilse, the Archmage's apprentice. You've chosen the Arcane road. Shall I show you how it works, properly, before you set something on fire? I'll lend you a wand and runes.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
The Archmage is busy, which is why you have me. I'm Ilse. Try to keep up.

The Arcane road: four elements, a wand or a staff, and the patience to read before you swing. Fire burns, water slows, earth breaks a guard, air topples. Every spell costs runes -- I've put a willow wand and a good stack of runes in your bag.
A wand in your hand. Without one, your spells stay in the book.
You take a few spells into a fight, in order, and cast the first you have runes for. Wind strike is air and mind runes. Choose your spells on the Combat tab -- more unlock as your Magic grows.
Runes run out. You make more at the rune shrines: carry essence stones to a shrine and each becomes a handful of runes. The Air shrine is in the Meadow.
Here are twenty essence stones. Go and craft some air runes -- every spell you know right now needs them.
Wands and staves are made at the altar in your Workshop: a willow wand is willow logs and quartz. Here are the makings.
steps.later: The altar isn't open to you yet. When it is, a willow wand is ten willow logs and five quartz -- keep these until then. Staves come later: air, water, earth and fire, each with its own runes.

say: When your bar fills: a Surge (one spell with everything you've got -- likelier to land, double damage) or a Burst (three spells at once, each paying its runes). Choose one.
Now read a creature. The Farmyard's hunting ground: win three fights with your spells. Watch what each element does to them.
Adequate. More than adequate, actually -- don't tell anyone I said so.

The Archmage wants me back at the tower before the stars turn. Take this: runes of every element, essence stones, a proper hat, and the Arcane's book. The Spellbook in your Library has every spell -- read it.

kit.name: Thief's starter crate
kit.about: Pip's parting gift: poisons, throwing knives, bandages and the Thief's book.

say: Pip. Don't look round. You've gone the Thief's way -- want the quick tour? I'll lend you the tools of the trade.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
Psst. Over here. Pip. Nell sent me -- her ledger walked off with some very angry people, and she'd like it back, so I haven't long.
A Thief fights with a dagger in each hand, or a bow, and poison on the blade. You're quick, you're quiet, and you're never where they swing. Two bronze daggers and three weak poisons are in your bag.
A dagger in each hand: one in your weapon slot, one in your off hand. Two blades, twice the chances for the poison to bite.
steps.goal: Hold a dagger in each hand

say: Now the trick. Coat your blades: open your bag and choose Coat your blades on the weak poison. A coating lasts for a number of hits, and now and then a hit poisons.

Poisons are brewed at the apothecary table: a weak poison is five mushrooms and five feverfew. Stronger ones want a venom sac, a scorpion's stinger, bat wings or wolfsbane -- the creatures carry them. Here are the makings of a weak one.
Throwing knives are a Thief's opener: they fly before the fight starts. One bronze bar makes a handful at the anvil.
Now the part Nell pays me for. Off the Village there's the Marketplace -- stalls, crowds, and pockets. That's Larceny: a skill of its own, and it stays yours whatever road you take later.

Go and lift a farmhand's purse. Quick hands, no staring. If you're caught it's a fine and a sore wrist, nothing worse -- but get caught three times in a quarter of an hour and Captain Hale throws you out for an hour.
steps.goal: Pick a pocket in the Marketplace

say: When your bar fills: a Backstab (more than double damage, daggers only), Envenom (your next hit poisons for sure) or a Smoke bomb (they miss for two rounds). Choose one on the Combat tab.
Right. The Farmyard's hunting ground. Win three -- and try not to be there when they swing.
Not bad. Not bad at all. Nell might even like you.

I've got a ledger to find before someone reads it. Here: poisons, throwing knives, bandages, the makings of more poison, a couple of venom sacs, and the Thief's book. Don't ask where any of it came from.

paladin.title: Paladin tutor
paladin.goodbye: Stand your ground, and the light stands with you.

kit.name: Paladin's starter crate
kit.about: Brother Aldo's parting gift: a kite shield, holy water and its makings, and the Paladin's book.

say: Brother Aldo. You've taken the Paladin's road. Let me show you how it's walked -- I'll lend you a sword, a shield and holy water.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
Peace be with you. Sister Maren keeps the chapel; I keep the door -- and today, you.
The Paladin's road: a sword, a shield, and devotion. Devotion grows each time you stand your ground, and it heals. A bronze sword, a wooden buckler and three flasks of holy water are in your bag.
The sword in your hand and the buckler in your off hand. A shield blocks some blows outright -- and every block is devotion earned.
steps.goal: Hold a sword and a shield

say: A buckler is two planks and soft leather at the crafting bench; kite shields are forged at the anvil. Make one -- you'll want a spare.
Holy water. Bless your blade with it -- from your bag -- and for thirty hits it strikes harder, and the undead fear it.
Holy water is made at the apothecary table: a silver bar, five lavender and a pot of water. Here are the makings of one flask.
steps.later: The apothecary isn't ready for holy water yet -- it wants some Alchemy behind it. Keep the silver, lavender and water; when you can, it's a silver bar, five lavender and a pot of water.

say: Devotion pays for Lay on hands (heal a third of your health), Smite (a holy blow -- three times as hard on the undead) or Aegis (nothing gets past your shield for three rounds). Choose one.
Now hold. The Farmyard's hunting ground -- win three fights. Block, and let devotion grow.
Well held. Maren will be glad to hear it.
The chapel door doesn't keep itself, and I've been away too long. Take this: a kite shield, holy water and the makings of more, bandages, and the Paladin's book. Go with the light.

beastmaster.title: Beast Master tutor

say: Tamsin. You've taken the lead -- shall I show you how a Beast Master works? I'll lend you two of my own pack to learn with.
Press Next and we'll start -- or Skip the lesson, and I'll still leave you a starter crate.
So you've taken the lead. Good. I'm Tamsin -- I run with a pack, and for a little while, so will you.

A Beast Master never swings a sword. Your battle pets fight, you choose their moves, feed them and swap them out -- and you never take a blow yourself. If every pet in the fight faints, you all go home.

You can't learn this with an empty pen, so I'll lend you two of mine: Bramble, my bear, and Hoot, my owl. They're in your Beast Pen now. I've put a crook, some grain feed and a few shrimps in your bag too.
First, the crook. It's a Beast Master's weapon: it adds to your pets' attack and lets you land a small blow of your own.
Open your Character sheet (your name at the top), then Gear, click the weapon slot on your figure and choose the oak crook.
Now the Beast Pen, at your Estate. Every battle pet lives in a stall there.

Each pet has a type -- Beast, Bird, Water, Reptile, Bug or Spirit -- strong against some creatures and weak to others; the Pen shows which. Pets level up from fights, and between fights they train one stat on their own: health, attack, defence or speed.
Put Bramble or Hoot on a stat to train.
steps.goal: Set a pet training in the Beast Pen

say: Training only happens while there's feed in the trough -- one grain feed or hay keeps a pet going for six hours, and the troughs hold a day.
Fill the troughs with the grain feed I gave you. Later you'll make your own at the Farm's Feed store.
Your pack is who comes hunting: the first fights, and up to two more wait on the bench and step in when one faints.
You choose it on your Character sheet's Combat tab. Add Bramble and Hoot.
steps.goal: Put a pet in your pack

say: Crooks are made at the crafting bench: oak logs and a rope. A better wood makes a better crook. Here are the makings -- make one.

Every pet learns its type's moves as it levels and uses up to four -- choose them on its card in the Pen. In a fight, pick a move for a pet and it keeps using it until you change it; leave it alone and it picks for itself.

In a fight you can also feed a hurt pet (that's its turn), swap in a pet from the bench, and fire a special when the bar fills: Command makes your front pet act twice, Rally heals the whole pack, and Wild call comes later.
A pet that faints rests in the Pen for a while. Food from your bag cuts its rest short.
Time to see them work. On the Map, open the Farmyard and click its hunting ground. Your pack does the fighting -- watch how they go, and try picking their moves.
Sorry, I have to depart now with my pack. Bramble and Hoot have earned a long run, and so have I.

I bid you good luck with starting your own pack. Take these two eggs as my parting gift: put them in the Hatchery, and when they hatch, send them to the Beast Pen -- it's free while they're new. And a crate for the road: feed, treats and the Beast Master's book.

beastmaster.goodbye: Good luck with your own pack!

kit.name: Beast Master's starter crate
kit.about: Tamsin's parting gift: feed, treats and the Beast Master's book.
